subject: Project Surge: onboarding additional teams, API keys, and term amendment
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tara Lim <tara.lim@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Project Surge: initial sizing & next steps

Tara —

Thanks again for the time last week. Based on the call notes, Atlas is preparing to expand the current footprint to three additional product teams (Search, Intake Forms, and Summaries) over the next two quarters. High level asks we captured: additional API keys for the teams, bump in committed throughput for evenings (peak), and a contract amendment to reflect a 12‑month renewal with the new committed units.

I put together a short proposal (attached) that shows the incremental pricing and a recommended staged rollout so your dev teams can test without impacting production traffic. Quick asks from our side to keep momentum:
- Confirm the list of projects that need keys (we used Search / Intake / Summaries)
- Confirm whether Procurement needs an SOW or just an amendment
- Preferred date window for the first key activation (we suggested week of Oct 26)

I’ll loop in Marissa on the rollout plan and Laura on contract language.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0172
[Attachment: Amendment_Proposal_ProjectSurge_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Tara Lim <tara.lim@atlashealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Chu <evan.chu@atlashealth.com>, Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Project Surge: initial sizing & next steps

Ben —

Thanks for the summary and the attachment. This aligns with what the product teams asked for. A couple of clarifications before we proceed:
1) Can you break out the pricing impact if we enable all 3 teams simultaneously vs. a two‑wave rollout (Search + Intake first, Summaries six weeks later)?
2) Procurement requests the amendment + an updated SLA reflecting evening peak latency targets for the triaged endpoints. Is that something you can include in the doc?
3) We will need 6 API keys initially (2 per team) — one for staging, one for prod.

Procurement (cc’d) — can you confirm whether Atlas needs a full SOW or if an amendment is sufficient for this expansion?

Best,
Tara
Head of Integrations | Atlas Health
tara.lim@atlashealth.com

Date: 2026-10-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Project Surge: initial sizing & next steps

Hi all —

Ben: I modeled both rollout options and attached a short table in the PDF. TL;DR: simultaneous enablement increases the committed units immediately and yields ~12% unit price reduction versus a staged approach because you lock more volume. Staged rollout keeps monthly commit lower during ramp but adds a small coordination overhead for key provisioning.

Tara: I added the evening latency SLO language to section 2.2 of the amendment draft. Marissa (me) and Laura can work with Procurement on the exact SLA phrasing.

Operational notes for keys and staging:
- We can issue 6 keys as requested. Recommended pattern: one service key per environment + one scoped key for cross-team shared tooling (makes rotation simpler).
- We can gate the prod keys behind a traffic-cutover checklist that includes canary traffic (5% for 48 hours) and KV prefix caching enabled in the runtime.

Proposed timeline:
- Week of Oct 26: issue staging keys + access docs
- Week of Nov 9: issue prod keys for Search + Intake after canary pass
- Week of Dec 1: issue prod keys for Summaries (if staged) or Dec 1 (if simultaneous)

Attaching the updated amendment and a short key onboarding doc.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Amendment_Proposal_ProjectSurge_v3.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: API_Key_Instructions_v1.docx (docx)]
